about: webcpp::hash's measured table (spec section 4.2): the size of one program per cell of doc/capabilities.json on each target, and its throughput, which detail/ranking.hpp orders the backends by. Written by tools/hash/measure.py --write; the documentation renders from it (ruling R21).

layout.schema: This description. The version of the layout is "version"; a change of layout raises it. Written only by tools/hash/measure.py; "digest" is the SHA-256 of the file without it, which the measure lane checks.
layout.date, machine, load_average_before_after: when and where the measurements were made; loaded says whether the machine was shared and loaded
layout.toolchains, runtimes, strip, pins, build: the compiler per target, wasmtime and node, the strip of the native sizes, each backend's library and pin (from doc/capabilities.json), and the two builds
layout.workloads: per function, what one computation does (spec 4.2)
layout.records[]: one per cell and target: operation (the function of doc/capabilities.json), hmac (or null), backend, target, size_bytes, result (the hexadecimal output, the same for every backend and target of an operation and hmac), throughput (repetitions, invocations, runs_per_invocation, invocation_medians_ns, median_ns, min_ns, max_ns: nanoseconds per computation) or null with throughput_absent saying why. operation, hmac, backend and target are the keys of doc/measurements.throughput.json's cases too, which the documentation joins on them (ruling R21); constant time is doc/capabilities.json's (ruling R26).
layout.orders[]: per operation, hmac and target: by_size and by_throughput, the backends that have it there in order, and throughput_from, the target whose throughput ordered it; detail/ranking.hpp is generated from the rows of the key derivations
layout.rules: how sizes, throughput and orders are made

rules.size: the bytes of the program built at variant=release optimization=space: natively the executable stripped with strip, on WebAssembly the .wasm file
rules.throughput: the program built at variant=release optimization=speed, run with --time: one computation to warm up, then five timed runs of the workload, each repeated `repetitions` times; per invocation the median of its five runs, per record the median of its invocations' medians, with the fastest and slowest run
rules.order: by size, a backend moves before the one ahead of it only when its program is smaller; by throughput, only when its median is more than 10 percent below the other's and its slowest run is faster than the other's fastest; otherwise the committed order stands (on a first measurement, the capability table's order of backends). A WebAssembly target orders by its own throughput where every backend of the row ran within the bound, else by the native order.
rules.loaded: the larger of the two 1-minute load averages exceeds the core count
